items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the banking law, in relation to removal and prohibition of
directors, trustees, officers, members or partners of certain entities; and to
repeal certain provisions of such law related thereto
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7532

SPONSOR: SANDERS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the banking law, in relation to removal and prohibition
of directors, trustees, officers, members or partners of certain enti-
ties; and to repeal certain provisions of such law related thereto

 
PURPOSE:

This bill would repeal the existing section 41 of the Banking Law
("BL"), dealing with the removal of officers, directors and trustees of
banking organizations, bank holding companies and foreign banks, and
enact a new BL § 41 that provides a clearer process for removing offi-
cers, directors and trustees, resolves longstanding issues with the
language of section 41, and expands the scope of the removal authority
to apply to all entities regulated by the Department of Financial
Services (the "Department") pursuant to the Banking Law.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill would repeal BL § 41 as it currently exists and
replace it with a new section 41 governing the removal of officers,
directors and trustees of entities regulated by the Department pursuant
to the BL. Subdivision 1 lists the regulated entities whose officers or
directors, defined as covered individuals, are subject to removal under
the revised section 41 and sets forth the grounds upon which an officer
or director may be removed.

Subdivision 2 provides for the notice and hearing process on a statement
of charges seeking to remove a covered person and provides that the
Superintendent may only issue an order removing a covered person if they
waive their right to a hearing, fail to appear at a hearing or if the
Superintendent finds that the covered individual engaged in conduct
identified in subdivision 1.

Subdivision 3 provides that the Department may suspend a covered indi-
vidual, pending the resolution of charges, if the Superintendent has
reason to believe that, by engaging in conduct specified in subdivision
1, a covered entity has or probably will suffer a financial loss, the
interests of the depositors of a covered institution are at issue, or
the covered individual demonstrates a willful disregard for the safety
and soundness of a covered entity.

Subdivision 4 provides that an order of suspension or removal becomes
effective when served on the covered individual and provides that any
covered individual who participates in the management of a covered enti-
ty after an order of suspension or removal has been served without the
permission of the Superintendent shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

Subdivision 5 provides that any order issued pursuant to BL § 41 may be
challenged pursuant to Article 78 of the Civil Practice Law and Rules.

Section 2 provides that the bill would take effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:


This bill would address long-standing anachronisms in BL § 41, update
the language to provide for clearer and expanded grounds for removal,
and grant the superintendent the authority to suspend an officer, direc-
tor or trustee in certain situations. In its current form, BL § 41
contemplates a process involving a board - the Banking Board - that has
not existed since the Department was created in 2011.  Removing the
references to the Banking Board is necessary to remove any possible
technical argument that any proceeding to remove an officer or director
was not initiated and overseen by a governing body that no longer
exists. In place of the Banking Board, the bill updates BL § 41 to refer
to the Superintendent of Financial Services.

The current version of BL § 41 also refers to violations of the BL as a
ground for removal. The BL, however, is generally addressed to the
conduct of regulated entities. To avoid any confusion as to the nature
of a predicate action necessary to justify the removal of an officer,
director or trustee, the bill provides that a covered person is subject
to removal when they participate, cause or facilitate, for example, a
violation of a covered entity. The bill further provides the Superinten-
dent with authority to suspend an officer, director or trustee when
there is reason to believe that such person is engaged in certain speci-
fied conduct that threatens the viability of an institution.

Finally, existing removal authority only applies to banking organiza-
tions, bank holding companies and branches of foreign banks.  The bill
provides that officers, directors and trustees of all entities regulated
by the Department are subject to removal if they engage in the conduct
identified in BL § 41.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

This bill will have no budget implications.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.

summary: Provides for the removal and prohibition of directors, trustees, officers, members or partners of certain entities.
